$ go test  # ladder-a
    the column parse is owned by . and ./b. Column names are unique per corpus root, and one package owns each column.

$ go test  # ladder-a-useonly
    the lift parse is used by . and ./b, and no package owns it, so its error is recorded nowhere.
        Own the lift in one of them: give it to hypercase.Own in place of hypercase.Use.
    testdata/script/x.txtar: no registry claims out/parse/outcome: no column named parse runs over the corpus script.
        If a column should write them, register the column. If not, delete them by hand; FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... leaves them in place.
